3.4.2.3-r1.burton_quote: and for four months, still raved, that she was in hell-fire, already damned

3.4.2.3-r11.burton_quote: the Queen of causes, and moderator of things, now she pulls down the proud

3.4.2.3-r2.burton_quote: If they be solitary given, superstitious, precise, or very devout: seldom shall you find a Merchant, a Soldier, an Innkeeper, a Bawd, an Host, an Usurer so troubled in mind, they have cheverel consciences that will stretch, they are seldom moved in this kind or molested: young men and middle age are more wild, and less apprehensive; but old folks

citations.display: Martin Luther, commentary on John, chapter 17

3.4.2.3-r3.translation: Not a few torment and torture themselves so much that they are not far from madness; and yet all they achieve by this anxiety of mind is to give the devil power to lead them through despair to hell.

3.4.2.3-r4.burton_quote: and do more harm in the Church (saith Erasmus) than they that flatter; great danger on both sides, the one lulls them asleep in carnal security, the other drives them to despair

citations.display: Erasmus, *Ecclesiastes* (*On the Art of Preaching*), book 1

3.4.2.3-r5.burton_quote: are still in their mouths, nothing but gall and horror, and a mad noise, they make all their auditors desperate
3.4.2.3-r5.translation: They rattle on horribly about the judgement to come and about damnation

3.4.2.3-r7.burton_quote: which tortures so many, that either out of a deep apprehension of their unworthiness, and consideration of their own dissolute life, accuse themselves and aggravate every small offence, when there is no such cause, misdoubting in the meantime God’s mercies, they fall into these inconveniences

3.4.2.3-r8.burton_quote: whoever saw (saith Chrysostom) a covetous man troubled in mind when he is telling of his money, an adulterer mourn with his mistress in his arms? We are then drunk with pleasure, and perceive nothing

3.4.2.3-r9.burton_quote: at last his conscience accused him, his unquiet soul could not rest day or night, he was terrified with fearful dreams, visions, and so miserably tormented all his life
